outcome.technical:
Added a SessionStart mode to the existing meter-usage.py hook (no new hook file): hooks.json now also wires meter-usage.py (open mode) on SessionStart. New function session_start_check(data, ul=None, cfg=None, root=None) finds the previous session's own transcript via a new usage_ledger.previous_session_transcript(data) helper (most-recently-modified sibling .jsonl beside the SessionStart payload's own transcript_path, excluded by session_id not by mtime/existence), reads that session's last assistant turn's model via the existing current_context_size, and checks usage_ledger.rates_for(model, table) - if the model has no price row, prints exactly one line naming the model and the usage.pricing remedy; otherwise silent. The message rides hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (not systemMessage), which is the one channel of this hook's output the model itself reads, routed in main() before meter() since a SessionStart payload's own transcript has no assistant turn yet to meter. Fails open (try/except returning None) on any missing/unreadable previous transcript, disabled config, or missing manifest.

A second check was implemented and then DROPPED before shipping, per the task's explicit measurement requirement: whether the previous session's CLI-reported cost-state (usage_ledger.read_cost_state, pre-existing from P125.4) disagrees with the ledger's own re-priced figure for that session (usage_ledger.cli_cost_divergences, also pre-existing), beyond CLI_COST_TOLERANCE_USD ($0.01). This was measured OFFLINE and READ-ONLY over every main-session transcript recorded under <home>/.claude/projects for this repo's own project directory and for the danuvia-software testbed project (neither transcript nor ledger directory was written to - only read.py/glob calls). Measurement commands (ad hoc, scratchpad-only, not committed): a short script loading usage_ledger.py by path, calling project_pricing(), current_context_size(), read_cost_state(), rates_for() and cli_cost_divergences() over every *.jsonl under each project's own <outside-repo><slug>/ directory, against each project's own real ledger (read via usage_ledger.read_ledger on the ledgerDir each project's own .claude/audit.config.json names).

Numbers (every one reproducible by re-running the commands named beside it):
- (a) start latency, `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py` after adding a 'sessionstart' LANES entry for meter-usage.py (the quiet/no-previous-session path, the common case): meter-usage.py/sessionstart measured at 50.49ms median of 9 (ratio 2.64x a bare interpreter start of 19.22ms) on this run - in the same range as the other 9 existing hook lanes (36-55ms, ratio 1.90x-2.87x on this run); this is NOT a gate per bench-hooks.py's own design (wall clock swings between repeats). `python3 tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` (the actual gate, the import-weight budget) stays green: exit 0, '10 hook(s) within budget' on all 6 interpreters found on this machine (3.8.20, 3.9.24, 3.10.19, 3.12.12, 3.13.12, 3.14.7) - meter-usage.py's module-level imports are unchanged, since the new code is a branch inside the same already-counted file.
- (b) bytes added to context: piping a real SessionStart JSON payload into `python3 plugins/audit/hooks/meter-usage.py` and measuring stdout with `wc -c`: a quiet start (previous session's model priced, or no previous session at all) writes 0 bytes to stdout; a firing start (previous session's model unpriced) writes 334 bytes, all of it the hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext JSON carrying one sentence.
- (c) offline benefit, read-only over recorded transcripts: this repo's own project directory held 13 main-session transcripts, the danuvia-software testbed held 18 (31 total). The SHIPPED check (unpriced model) would have fired on 2 of the 31 (one per project) - both were sessions whose last assistant turn named model '<synthetic>' (a test/eval artifact, not a real model the price table was ever expected to carry), silent on the other 29. The DROPPED check (cost-state divergence) was also measured on the same 31 transcripts against each project's real ledger: divergent (model, session) pairs existed in both projects; grouping them by model and looking at the CLI/plugin cost RATIO across every session that model diverged in - the test a single static mispriced rate would have to pass (a constant ratio) - only one model (2 sessions, in danuvia-software) held a near-constant ratio; every other model measured (7 distinct models across both projects, session counts of 1-11) scattered across a wide range session to session, and a meaningful share of the divergent pairs had no ledger row recorded for that session/model at all (metering gap, not a priced disagreement). A scattered ratio is not explained by one wrong rate, and matches the shape usage_ledger.read_cost_state's own pre-existing docstring documents on this repo's own transcripts (conversation compaction trimming the retained .jsonl while the CLI's cumulative total does not shrink, or a subagent spending outside what got scanned). Per the orchestrator's explicit instruction ('If divergence fires mostly for causes other than a stale price, ship only the unpriced-model check... that outcome is a success, not a failure'), the divergence check was left unwired; session_start_check's own docstring records this reasoning (with no numbers in it, per the house rule) and points to this return for the measurement.
